question: Find the HCF of 44, 110 and 198.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The HCF of given numbers always divides the difference between any two of them.

Difference between 110 and 44 = 66.

The HCF must be a factor of 66 (i.e., 66, 33, 22, 11, etc.).

Checking the highest possible factor 22: 44, 110, and 198 are all completely divisible by 22.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 44, 110, and 198.

**Method Used:**

Prime factorization method. The HCF is the product of the smallest powers of common prime factors.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 44 = 2 × 2 × 11 = 2² × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 110 = 2 × 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 198 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 11 = 2 × 3² × 11

⇒ Common prime factors are 2 and 11.

⇒ Lowest power of 2 is 2¹ and lowest power of 11 is 11¹.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 11

⇒ HCF = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

LCM is the smallest number that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by taking the highest powers of all prime factors involved.

Difference Method for HCF

The HCF of any two or more numbers cannot be greater than the difference between any two of the numbers. It is always a factor of their difference.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is exactly 1. They do not have any common prime factors.
